claims.claim: July 1805, Anna Pávlovna Schérer, maid of honor, reception; Prince Vasíli first to arrive
claims.evidence: 'It was in July, 1805... Anna Pávlovna Schérer, maid of honor... Prince Vasíli Kurágin... the first to arrive at her reception'

claims.claim: talk of Napoleon, war, match for Anatole
claims.evidence: 'this means war'; 'Have you never thought of marrying your prodigal son Anatole?'

claims.claim: Pierre illegitimate son of count, inherits
claims.evidence: 'an illegitimate son of Count Bezúkhov'; 'will become Count Bezúkhov, and will then inherit'

claims.claim: Pierre marries Hélène; duel with Dólokhov
claims.evidence: 'Pierre felt that Hélène... must be his wife'; 'Dólokhov's duel with Bezúkhov'
'Prince Andrew, with others fatally wounded, was left to the care of the inhabitants'
'Prince Andrew had loved his wife, she died'

claims.claim: engaged to Natásha, drawn to Anatole
claims.evidence: 'After Prince Andrew's engagement to Natásha'; 'Natásha had made a strong impression on Kurágin'
'Natásha's note to Princess Mary breaking off her engagement'; 'his betrothed had broken faith with him'
claims.fix: her note to Princess Mary breaks off the engagement

claims.evidence: Pierre at Raévski's battery; 'I am your prisoner—take me!'

claims.claim: Andrew mortally wounded at Borodinó, dies with Natásha and Mary
claims.evidence: 'Prince Andrew is here, mortally wounded'; 'Natásha put down the stocking...'; 'Prince Andrew died'; Mary arrived

claims.claim: Moscow burns, French retreat; Pétya killed
claims.evidence: 'Pétya fell heavily... A bullet had pierced his skull.'

claims.claim: Pierre marries Natásha; Nicholas marries Mary
claims.evidence: 'In the winter of 1813 Nicholas married Princess Mary'; 'Natásha had married in the early spring of 1813'

claims.claim: Hélène Pierre's first wife, Vasíli's daughter; died
